slides.title: Welcome to Transitions & Animations
slides.content:
# CSS Transitions & Animations 🎬

Motion transforms static websites into interactive, polished experiences. Smooth micro-interactions provide intuitive feedback and delight users.

## What you'll master:
- 🔄 **CSS Transitions** - Property interpolation, duration, and delays
- 📉 **Easing Timing Functions** - `ease`, `linear`, `cubic-bezier()`, and natural physics
- 📐 **Hardware-Accelerated 2D/3D Transforms** - `translate`, `scale`, `rotate`
- 🎞️ **Keyframe Animations (`@keyframes`)** - Multi-stage animation sequences
- ⚡ **Animation Performance** - GPU acceleration and `prefers-reduced-motion`

slides.title: Transitions: Animating State Changes
Transition Individual Properties
Transition Timing Functions (Easing)
slides.content:
# Timing Functions & Easing Curves 📉

Easing controls the acceleration and deceleration rate of an animation:

```
Speed
  ▲
  │     /─────\         ease-in-out (Slow start, fast middle, slow end)
  │    /         │   /           └───┴──────────┴───► Time
```

- `ease` *(Default)*: Slow start, fast middle, slow end.
- `linear`: Constant speed from start to finish.
- `ease-in`: Starts slow, accelerates to a sudden stop.
- `ease-out`: Starts fast, decelerates to a gentle stop (best for UI clicks/hovers!).
- `cubic-bezier(p1, p2, p3, p4)`: Custom mathematical Bézier curve.

slides.title: 2D Transforms: Translate, Scale, Rotate
Why Transforms Beat Margins for Animation
slides.content:
# Performance: Transforms vs Top/Margin ⚡

Why should you **never** animate `margin-top` or `top` for button hovers?

- **Animating `top` / `margin`:** Triggers browser **Layout** (Reflow) and **Repaint**, forcing the browser to recalculate the entire page geometry 60 times per second! Causes jank and stutter.
- **Animating `transform` & `opacity`:** Handled directly on the **GPU** (Compositor thread)! Zero layout reflow, guaranteeing buttery smooth 60fps/120fps motion.

slides.title: Animation Fill Mode (forwards vs backwards)
slides.content:
# The Critical `animation-fill-mode` 🎬

When an animation finishes, by default the element snaps right back to its original pre-animation styling. `animation-fill-mode` controls state before and after:

- `none` *(Default)*: Retains no styles from the animation outside its duration.
- `forwards`: The element **keeps the styles of the final keyframe (100%)** after finishing!
- `backwards`: Applies the 0% styles during any initial `animation-delay`.
- `both`: Applies backwards before start, and forwards after finish!

```css_not
.fade-in-slide {
  animation: slideUp 0.6s ease-out forwards; /* Stays visible at final position! */
}
```

slides.title: Respecting prefers-reduced-motion
The will-change Property
3D Transforms: Flipping Cards
Animation Performance Checklist
slides.content:
# Animation Performance Rules 🏁

1. **Only animate `transform` and `opacity`:** These properties run on the GPU compositor without triggering layout reflows.
2. **Never animate `width`, `height`, `margin`, `top`, or `left`.**
3. **Keep durations between 150ms and 350ms:** Faster than 150ms feels abrupt; slower than 400ms feels sluggish to users.
4. **Always include `prefers-reduced-motion`:** Accessibility is mandatory.

slides.title: Summary & Next Steps
slides.content:
# Transitions & Animations Mastered! 🌟

You can now build rich, 60fps hardware-accelerated animations and micro-interactions!

## Key Takeaways:
- ✅ **Transitions:** Smoothly interpolate property changes (duration, timing, delay).
- ✅ **Transforms:** Use `translate`, `scale`, and `rotate` for GPU performance.
- ✅ **Keyframes:** Define complex multi-step sequences with `@keyframes`.
- ✅ **`animation-fill-mode: forwards`:** Preserves final state when animation completes.
- ✅ **Accessibility:** Honor `prefers-reduced-motion` for motion-sensitive users.
